title: Minister’s decisions, 8 October 2026 — visible decision section
text:
Review of measures for shore-based shellfish harvesting in the Auckland-Coromandel area
UPDATES
8 October 2026: Minister’s decisions announced

Following this consultation, the Minister for Oceans and Fisheries has made decisions on sustainability measures for shellfish in the Auckland-Coromandel area.

These decisions include:

closing a defined intertidal zone to recreational harvesting activities, with exceptions for certain shellfish species
setting reduced daily limits for some species in areas that remain open to harvest.

Minister for Oceans and Fisheries decision letter [PDF, 588 KB]
Fact sheet: New shellfish rules for Auckland and Coromandel [PDF, 1.1 MB]

In a few weeks, we will release the advice paper we prepared for the minister.

Summary of the minister's decisions

These decisions apply from 1 November 2026.

Recreational harvesting of invertebrates, except for named species of shellfish, will be prohibited in a defined intertidal closure area. Invertebrates are species without a backbone which includes all shellfish and other marine life such as anemones and sponges.
The intertidal closure will apply from the mean high-water mark (that is, the landward boundary) to a point offshore where the water is 2 metres deep (that is, the seaward boundary).
The seaward boundary of the intertidal closure will move as the tide goes in and out – refer to images in the fact sheet.
The intertidal closure area will apply to a specified area on the Auckland-Coromandel mainland extending from Cape Rodney to Houmanga Point (north of Waihi Beach) on the east coast and from Ōkiritoto Stream on Muriwai Beach to Port Waikato on the west coast. The closure will also apply to the Waiheke Island coastline.
New recreational daily limits will apply to certain species of shellfish. Refer to Table 1.
Table 1: Auckland-Coromandel intertidal closure and daily limits that will apply from 1 November 2026

Daily limits that have changed are marked with an asterix (*).

The intertidal zone is from the mean high-water mark to a point offshore where the water is 2 metres deep.

Existing shellfish closures will remain in force. It is important that fishers check the rules before they harvest in a particular area.

As a result of consultation and further analysis undertaken by Fisheries New Zealand, the proposed intertidal closure offshore boundary was amended to reflect a 2-metre depth-based boundary. The 2-metre depth boundary aligns better with the intertidal zone to manage harvesting pressure in areas that are most accessible at low tide, without impacting peoples’ access to shellfish in subtidal areas.
